title: Determining prenatal, early childhood and cumulative long-term lead exposure using micro-spatial deciduous dentine levels.
ehr_evidence: Mother–child pairs in this study were drawn from the longitudinal birth cohort studies in Mexico City that comprise the Early Life Exposures in MExico and NeuroToxicology (ELEMENT) project.
summary: Validation study assessing micro-spatial dentine lead levels as a biomarker for accurately estimating prenatal, early childhood, and long-term cumulative lead exposure by comparing them with maternal blood, bone, cord blood, and serial childhood blood samples.
key_findings: Dentine Pb at birth significantly associated with cord blood Pb (Spearman r = 0.69; n = 27; p<0.0001).
Prenatal dentine Pb associated with maternal patella Pb (r = 0.48; n = 59; p<0.0001) and tibia Pb (r = 0.35; n = 41; p<0.03).
Dentine Pb at 3 months significantly associated with concurrent child blood Pb (r = 0.64; n = 55; p<0.0001).
Secondary dentine Pb correlated positively with cumulative blood lead index (CBLI) (r = 0.38; n = 75; p<0.0007).
Birth dentine Pb not significantly associated with child blood Pb after 2 years of age.
Secondary dentine Pb correlations with maternal bone and blood during pregnancy were weaker and statistically insignificant.
population: 85 mother-child pairs from the ELEMENT cohort in Mexico City, children followed from birth to 6-11 years
limitations: Incomplete biomarker data on all participants due to incomplete follow-up and sample collection
Only one tooth per participant analyzed, preventing assessment of tooth type influence
Small sample sizes for some specific comparisons
